title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Rheingau and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show producer, village plus vineyard, like Rüdesheimer Berg Rottland, the grape, the Prädikat or trocken, and the VDP eagle if a member. GG means dry top-site wine. Erstes Gewächs was the Rheingau's older term for top dry wines. Spätburgunder from Assmannshausen is labelled as red.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Dry Rheingau Riesling suits pork, veal, river fish like trout and pike, white asparagus, a German spring favourite, and schnitzel. Off-dry and Spätlese suit spicy food and roast pork. Spätburgunder suits game birds and mushrooms. Serve Riesling at 8 to 11 degrees.

steps.prompt: Which German spring vegetable suits dry Rheingau Riesling?
steps.explanation: Spargel season is a German ritual.

steps.body: Good Rheingau GG Riesling ages 10 to 20 years, developing honey, toast and petrol notes while keeping its acidity.

steps.prompt: GG wines from the VDP are sweet.
steps.explanation: Not true. GG wines are dry.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show vineyard, Prädikat or trocken, and the VDP eagle
Dry Riesling suits asparagus, trout and pork
